decisions.quote: In our most recent work (Busner et al., 2024 ), we examined the calibration of the optimized forms against the full-length version at common study inclusion thresholds (i.e., equivalent to full-length PANSS scores of 60 and 120) and found that the optimized forms showed minimal discrepancies compared with the 30-item form. The current work presents the first replication of this important finding, again using multisite international clinical trial data. In addition to examining these inclusion thresholds, the current work evaluates the performance of the PANSS10 and PANSS20 short forms in terms of measurement model fit, reliability of the scores, and content coverage relative to the PANSS30.

raw_expert_opinion.reason: Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are absent for this work. (1) Empirical retesting: Using independent pediatric clinical trial data from Savitz et al. (2015; N = 228), the source explicitly states that it conducts the first replication of the Busner et al. (2024) finding that the PANSS10 and PANSS20 show minimal calibration discrepancies against the 30-item PANSS at common trial inclusion thresholds (scores of 60 and 120, or item averages of 2 and 4), testing this via Bland-Altman analyses in Results and confirming in the Discussion that overall results support Busner et al. (2024) in content coverage, reliability, validity, and calibration. (2) Source-backed identity: The reference list identifies 'Busner J, Youngstrom EA, Langfus JA, et al. Replicating and extending the reliability, criterion validity, and treatment sensitivity of the shortened PANSS for pediatric trials. European Child & Adolescent Psychiatry 2024. in press.' with no DOI printed in the source. (3) Absence and non-equivalence: The sole shipped row (input_row_index 630) is Findling et al. (2023, J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry, 10.1016/j.jaac.2022.07.864), which initially developed the PANSS10/PANSS20 in NIMH TEOSS data and did not report the Busner et al. (2024) inclusion-threshold calibration analysis. Busner et al. (2024) is also distinct from sibling target_index 2 (Youngstrom et al., 2024, JAACAP Open, 10.1016/j.jaacop.2024.02.010), as the authors explicitly distinguish the two papers and refer to Busner et al. (2024), Findling et al. (2023), and Youngstrom et al. (2024) as three separate previous studies.

raw_expert_opinion.quote: The results presented in this study evaluated these optimized forms in data from an additional independent randomized pediatric schizophrenia trial (Savitz et al., 2015 ). Overall, these results support three previous studies showing that the PANSS10 and PANSS20 compare favorably to the 30-item PANSS in terms of content coverage, reliability, validity, and calibration, with a significant reduction in administration length (Busner et al., 2024 ; Findling et al., 2023 ; Youngstrom et al., 2024 ).
raw_expert_opinion.reason: Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are absent for this work. Luna's 'not_a_target' triage is overruled because it focused solely on a limitation note that placebo-vs-active treatment discrimination could not be assessed without a placebo arm, overlooking the psychometric and longitudinal claims explicitly retested from Youngstrom et al. (2024). (1) Empirical retesting: In Methods ('Statistical analyses'), the authors explicitly state that their confirmatory factor analyses (CFA) 'assessed the fit of the five-factor models for the PANSS10 and PANSS20 identified in previous work (Findling et al., 2023 ; Youngstrom et al., 2024 )', and in Results and Discussion they evaluate omega and IRT score reliability, content coverage correlations with the PANSS30, baseline criterion validity with CGI-S, and longitudinal sensitivity to change from baseline (eta-squared), concluding that their results 'support three previous studies showing that the PANSS10 and PANSS20 compare favorably to the 30-item PANSS in terms of content coverage, reliability, validity, and calibration, with a significant reduction in administration length (Busner et al., 2024 ; Findling et al., 2023 ; Youngstrom et al., 2024 ).' (2) Source-backed identity: Verified in the reference list and Crossref metadata as Youngstrom EA, Langfus JA, Daniel DG, et al. (2024), 'Replicating and extending the reliability, criterion validity, and treatment sensitivity of the PANSS10 and PANSS20 for pediatric trials', JAACAP Open, DOI 10.1016/j.jaacop.2024.02.010. (3) Absence and non-equivalence: Shipped row 630 is Findling et al. (2023, 10.1016/j.jaac.2022.07.864), the initial TEOSS scale-development paper, and sibling target_index 0 is Busner et al. (2024, European Child & Adolescent Psychiatry); the source explicitly treats Findling et al. (2023), Youngstrom et al. (2024), and Busner et al. (2024) as three distinct prior empirical studies.
